title: Monotonicity of the depth-threshold probability
statement: Fix a parameter $p$ with $0 \le p \le 1$, a Boolean function $f : (\mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \mathrm{Bool}) \to \mathrm{Bool}$, and thresholds $l_1 \le l_2$. Under a Bernoulli($p$) random restriction $\rho$ on the $n$ variables, the probability that the restricted function $x \mapsto f(\rho.\mathrm{extend}\,x)$ has decision-tree depth strictly greater than $l_2$ is at most the probability that it has decision-tree depth strictly greater than $l_1$.
hypotheses_covered: f a Boolean function on n variables
replaced:
For $0\le p\le 1$, a Boolean function $f$, and thresholds $l_1\le l_2$, the probability that
the restricted function exceeds depth $l_2$ is at most the probability that it exceeds depth
$l_1$.
